newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open ahead, strong dollar cited.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open ahead, strong dollar cited.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices opened higher on Monday in line with overseas gains.
Analysts said demand for dollar-denominated securities came from the Far East as the dollar strengthened against the yen following the election in Japan.

"Strength in the dollar helped support gains in Treasuries overnight" after the victory of the Liberal Democratic Party in Japan "indicated that Japan's low rate policy would prolong the yen's weak trend," said analysts at MMS International.
"The Japanese elections have not helped the yen and there's some Far East demand for U.S. securities related to the dollar's strength," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A.
But Stiles said New York could have a hard time adding much to the early gains becaue of upcoming supply in the two- and five-year sector.
The Treasury will sell $18.25 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday in its monthly two- and five-year note auctions.
In initial trade, the benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year bond was up as much as 5/32, but soon after, it was up only 2/32 to 99-14/32, yielding 6.79 percent.
"Gains will be capped by caution ahead of supply coming on Tuesday and Wednesday," said Stiles.

"We look for range trading, more or less," said James Blumenthal, economist at MCM Moneywatch. "There's no economic data coming out today so the focus is the auctions tomorrow and Wednesday," he said. "Supply is the most immediate concern now."
The Treasury will also sell $26.0 billion in three- and six-month Treasury bills at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
Stiles said whatever selling pressure emerges "will probably come from the underwriting side, rather than the investor side.

"I don't sense that investors are lining up to book profits on Monday, but underwriters want to adjust positions," said Stiles. "If they sell a little ahead of time, they can just cover their shorts and have a bid. You might see that trade developing either late this afternoon or tomorrow morning."
In early trade, three-month bill rates were unchanged at 4.98 percent. Six-month bill rates were up one basis point to 5.10 percent. Year bill rates were unchanged at 5.23 percent.
Two-year notes were unchanged at 100-7/32, yielding 5.88 percent. The 6.375 percent five-year note was up 1/32 at 100-18/32 to yield 6.24 percent.
The 6.5 percent ten-year note was up 1/32 at 100 even to yield 6.50 percent.

In when-issued trade, the two-year notes to be auctioned on Tuesday were yielding 5.895 percent. The five-year notes to be sold on Wednesday were yielding 6.245 percent in when-issued trade. -- 212-859-1679
